text: This is Skywalker. A game engine built for AI agents.
We gave a crew of AI agents twelve game ideas, and filmed them building every one, live, inside the editor.
A director plans. A level designer builds. A lighting artist sets the mood. A gameplay programmer brings it to life. Every edit is real, attributed, and undoable.
Horror. Fog that pools on the ground, a lantern that flickers, and three hundred meters down, something with a light of its own.
Or something cozy. A cabin on a snowy night. A harvest fair at golden hour. An aurora over the igloo.
Shooters, where every bolt, drone, and explosion is a prefab, spawned by a few lines of Wander.
Platformers in three D and two D. And a kart race under the floodlights.
And pure atmosphere. A zen garden in the morning mist. A neon alley in the rain.
Under the hood, a new renderer. Physically based materials, image based lighting, soft shadows, ambient occlusion, and a real sky, from afternoon to starlight. Or flip it to toon.
Agents generate seamless textures on demand. Bricks, wood, rust, marble, scales.
Everything is an asset they can search, preview, reuse, and scatter. Import models from glTF, OBJ, PLY, and STL.
They can even fetch openly licensed models from the web, with your approval. Licenses and credits are tracked for you.
Design your crew. Their roles, instructions, permissions, and memory. Run them alone, together, or in parallel.
Bring Claude, GPT, or a model on your own machine. Through MCP, any agent can drive the engine.
